content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text addresses a challenger's chain read together and considers its footing before noting the challenged sentence's own support, rather than demanding that one pressed verse state the contrary.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires","room":"by footing, never verse by verse: I weighed whether it bars only demanding one pressed witness state the contrary, or bars any use of the challenged sentence's own words; the rule's context supports the former.","why":"The judge recognized the challenger's analogy as footed and used Matthew 1:20's own support, not a requirement that a single pressed verse state the contrary, so it does not apply the retired stating-verse test."}
